diningPos.h1: Restaurant POS that keeps peaks steady and chains in control
diningPos.lead: When you search for restaurant POS, don't only compare hardware prices. The real gap is peak stability, kitchen clarity, inventory accuracy, and HQ menu sync. TAKOPOS is built for F&B operations.
diningPos.whatBody1: A restaurant POS is more than a cash register. It connects ordering, kitchen tickets, checkout, loyalty, inventory, and reports. Done well, peaks are calmer and closing is cleaner.
diningPos.whatBody2: Modern systems also need QR ordering, KDS, e-invoicing, and chain HQ controls. TAKOPOS focuses on real floor workflows from store one to store N.

q1.q: How is restaurant POS different from retail POS?
q1.a: Restaurants need tables, add-ons, kitchen routing, and peak tempo—far more than scan-and-pay retail checkout.

q2.q: Do small shops need a restaurant POS?
q2.a: If you already have busy peaks, delivery, or expansion plans, systemizing earlier avoids a full rip-and-replace later.

q3.a: It depends on menu complexity and hardware. Success is measured by clean kitchen flow and staff readiness, not just a date.

q4.q: Why do chains need restaurant POS more?
q4.a: Multi-store pain is menu drift, siloed inventory, and blind HQ. A good POS pushes decisions storewide.

q5.a: Hotpot, Chinese dining, hybrids, and stores that need QR/tableside or kitchen routing. Book a demo with your menu to confirm.

q6.q: Can we try before we buy?
q6.a: Yes. Leave your store details and our team will arrange a walkthrough around your peak scenarios.

chooseDiningPos.h1: How to choose a restaurant POS: compare these 8 things first
chooseDiningPos.lead: Searching restaurant POS brings many vendors. Most regrets come from broken peaks and kitchens, not sticker price. Use this comparison lens before you buy.
chooseDiningPos.mistakesLead: Skip these so the spec sheet does not choose for you.

m1.title: Comparing only hardware price
m1.body: Cheap terminals with weak software still fail at rush. Include fees, onboarding, training, and expansion.

m2.title: Judging by pretty admin screenshots
m2.body: Owners see reports; servers and kitchens decide outcomes. Ask for a demo with your menu.

m3.title: Longer feature lists win
m3.body: Unused modules create training drag. Check if ordering, kitchen, inventory, and chain truly connect.

m4.title: Ignoring store two
m4.body: Single-store success ≠ HQ menu push and multi-store stock. Compare expansion early.
